## Effekter og implementering

- Farver og fonte kommer fra brandet og tokeninputtet. Nye nødvendige farvepar genereres og måles i tokenlaget; ingen nye hex-værdier i komponent-/brand-/design-CSS.
- Behold tekst, formularer og vigtige tal på kendte, opake tokenflader. Ved transparens: test værste baggrund, ikke ét frame. Sørg for opak fallback ved manglende blur og fungerende kontroller i forced colors.
- Dekoration får `aria-hidden="true"`, `pointer-events: none` og ingen tab-stop. Ingen betydning kun i effekten.
- Brug højst ét vedvarende dekorativt bevægelseslag. Stop ved reduced motion, skjult dokument og uden for viewport. Giv pause/stop ved automatisk bevægelse over fem sekunder. Ingen blink eller lysglimt.
- Foretræk CSS/SVG frem for tunge afhængigheder. Video/WebGL kræver et konkret behov og statisk fallback; navigation og læsning virker uden effekten.
- Brug scenemotoren til slides/introer. En almindelig landingsside skal reflowe; læg ikke dens tekst/formularer på en nedskaleret 1920×1080-flade.
- Indfør ikke fiktive live-signaler, resultater, anmeldelser eller partnerlogoer for at fylde et layout. Mærk eksempler tydeligt.

layout-eksemplet i `starter-design-css.md` giver egne kompositionsgreb til `clean`, `modern-saas`, `editorial`, `dashboard` og `workspace` plus `.page-heading`, `.split-layout`, `.metric-grid` og `.bento`. Aktivér kun den valgte opskrift med `data-design` på html; tilføj klasser efter indholdet. Ingen opskrift vælger farver, fonte eller tema. Resten af kataloget er vejledning, ikke CSS-implementationer.

# Komposition og visuel kvalitet

Denne reference gælder kun brugerens genererede app og kun inden for den konkret godkendte opgave. Den ændrer ikke værtsappen Aura, dens onboarding, planer eller godkendelser.


Læs efter brand discovery sammen med designretningen. Et teknisk gyldigt skærmbillede er udgangspunktet; slutresultatet skal hjælpe en konkret bruger og have en tydelig afsender.

## Form skærmen efter opgaven

1. Skriv den vigtigste brugeropgave og næste handling. Gør det tydeligt: Hvor er jeg? Hvad kan jeg gøre? Hvad sker der bagefter?
2. Fordel plads mellem navigation, opgaveoverskrift, hovedindhold og hjælp. Giv hovedopgaven mest vægt; undgå en stor marketinghero foran en daglig arbejdsopgave.
3. Brug kort til indhold med sin egen enhed/handling. Brug rækker, lister, sektioner og linjer til sammenhængende indhold. Hver flade skal have et formål.
4. Prioritér efter betydning, ikke efter tomme pladser i en skabelon. Færre KPI'er med en klar beslutning er bedre end et stort gitter uden formål.
5. Vælg ét særkende, brandet tillader: et eksisterende farvebånd, typografisk detalje, sektionsrytme eller relevant diagram. Kopiér ikke inspirationssidens produktidentitet.

## Rytme, typografi og tæthed

- Definér titel, sektionsoverskrift, brødtekst, label og hjælp én gang med tokens; tilpas ikke størrelser enkeltvis for at fylde huller.
- Brug mindre afstand inden for grupper end mellem dem. Align tekst, felter og handlinger til få fælles linjer.
- Behold mindst 16px brødtekst og fluid displaytype. Gør ikke vigtige labels til bittesmå versaler for at efterligne en stil.
- Vælg tæthed efter opgaven. En eksperttabel kan være tættere end en vejledning, men klikflader og læsbarhed består. Luft skal hjælpe scanning uden at gøre et enkelt flow unødigt langt.
- Brug tabular-nums og ens enheder til sammenligninger. Tilføj kun diagrammer, der besvarer et reelt spørgsmål.
- Brug ét sammenhængende, bundtet ikonsæt. Ikoner supplerer labels; vigtig betjening må ikke kun forklares ved hover.

## Tilpas kompositionen

| Leverance | Prioritering | Undgå |
|---|---|---|
| Arbejdsapp | Overskrift/handling → filtre → opgave → hjælp | Stor intro, dekorative KPI'er, et kort om hvert felt. |
| Dashboard | Spørgsmål/periode → vigtigste mål → sammenligning → detaljer | Pyntediagrammer, uens tidsskalaer, betydning kun i farve. |
| Landingsside | Konkret værdi → løsning i brug → dokumentation → næste skridt | Fiktive anmeldelser, generisk hero, samme kortgitter overalt. |
| Læseside | Titel/indledning → indhold → relevant navigation | Smal tekst klemt mellem stor pynt, displayfont på alle labels. |
| Slides | Én pointe → tydelig scene → kilde/noter | Små afsnit skaleret ned, animation som eneste forklaring. |

## Adfærd er en del af finish

- Design default, hover, fokus, aktiv, valgt, disabled, loading og fejl. Fokus skal være tydeligt og ikke skjules af sticky elementer.
- Beskriv klik, ventetid, afbrydelse og fejl. Bevar input ved fejl og giv en konkret vej videre. Dekoration må ikke simulere aktivitet.
- Behold de fire visningstilstande fra app-patterns.md. Stress indholdet med nul, ét og mange resultater, lange danske ord og fejl på flere linjer.
- Ved AI: saml prompt, datagrænse og primær handling. Hold resultat, kilder, stop og avancerede muligheder forståelige. Påstå kun lokal/EU-behandling, når det er verificeret.

## Responsivitet og tilgængelighed

- Definér mobilrækkefølgen først. DOM-rækkefølgen er læse-/fokusrækkefølge; undgå dense grid eller CSS order, som skjuler en forkert struktur.
- Kontrollér 320px, QA-bredderne og 200 % zoom. Ingen skjulte handlinger eller afskåret tekst. Tabeller kan have en forklaret, fokuserbar scrollregion.
- Test understøttede temaer med hover, fejl, fokus og langt indhold. Stilvalg ændrer aldrig automatisk brugerens temavalg.
- Reduced motion: indhold, status og navigation virker uden animation. Forced colors: kontroller og valgt/fokuseret tilstand forsvinder ikke med baggrunde og skygger.
- Mål nye farvepar på faktiske flader. At to farver er tokens gør dem ikke automatisk egnede sammen; fx er muted tekst ikke nødvendigvis sikker på en primærfarvet flade.

## Kvalitetsport før aflevering

Se screenshots i fuld størrelse og ved siden af den officielle afsenderreference. Notér konkrete observationer i `qa/design-review.md`; skriv ikke bare "ser godt ud".

| Kontrol | Bestået når |
|---|---|
| Identitet | Logo, palette, fonte og former kan føres tilbage til BRAND.md; fravalg forklares. |
| Hierarki | Hovedopgave/handling er tydelig; hjælp konkurrerer ikke med den. |
| Komposition | Grupper, alignments og afstandsskala hænger sammen; flader har et formål. |
| Typografi | Hierarkiet gentages, og tekst/tal/labels kan læses i relevante visninger. |
| Interaktion | Kontroltilstande og alle fire visningstilstande virker med tastatur og mus/touch. |
| Robusthed | Langt indhold, mobil, zoom, tema og reduced motion bevarer indhold og funktion. |
| Særkende | Designet har en konkret relation til afsenderen og opgaven. |

Ret konkrete svagheder inden for den godkendte opgave og forklar uafklarede punkter. Ændring af en allerede godkendt designretning kræver konkret accept. Dette er en manuel vurdering, ikke en automatisk score eller juridisk godkendelse. Rapportér kun faktisk kørt QA; der medfølger intet installeret qa.py-script.

Kildeskillens dokumenterede inspirationskilder er bevaret; eventuelle aktuelle vilkår skal verificeres særskilt før senere konkret import.

Starterfiler, designbrief og valgfrit layoutlag er læsbare Markdown-eksempler, som først må materialiseres gennem godkendte filhandlinger. Den tidligere sikre demonstration bevares: ingen backend, login eller varig sagslagring; ingen ubetroet SVG indsættes som HTML; brugerinput renderes som tekst. CSS-layoutets udefinerede `--t-hero` er erstattet af generatorens `--t-3xl`. Hårdkodet hvid tekst på farebaggrund erstattes af et målt `text-on-danger`-token. Tokeneksemplet validerer input og viser de konkrete målte par i begge temaer; det er ingen generel WCAG-garanti. Det installeres eller køres ikke automatisk.

## Bevidst udeladte programmer

- `scripts/brand_scan.py`: originalen kan hente vilkårlige URLer og redirects uden Auras destinationskontrol og uden en fast downloadgrænse. Designkilder tilgås i stedet med eksisterende tilladte værktøjer.
- `scripts/qa.py`: originalen kan hente ekstern, ikke hashbundet testkode, servere hele en målmappe, følge symlinks og afslutte uden fuld dækning af de lovede kontroller. Adapteren bruger konkrete allerede godkendte lokale kontroller og angiver manglende prøver som uafprøvede.

`scripts/make_tokens.py` inkluderes ikke som eksekverbar fil. Generatorreferencen er en tilpasset offlinekodeversion til frivillig, separat materialisering og godkendt kørsel i brugerprojektet. Ingen `scripts/`- eller `assets/`-mappe følger med i biblioteket, og ingen Python-, browser-, CDN- eller npm-afhængighed tilføjes.

# Offentlige løsninger: afklar krav før drift

Dette er design- og afklaringsvejledning, adapteret fra kildens oktober 2026-version. Det er ikke juridisk rådgivning, en sikkerhedsgodkendelse eller bevis på efterlevelse. Den konkrete organisation skal afklare gældende standarder, målgruppe, data, behandlingsgrundlag og drift. Slå kun aktuelle kilder op, hvis projektets netværks- og datatilladelser giver adgang; ellers markér vurderingen som uafklaret.

## Tilgængelighed

Offentlige websteder og apps kan være omfattet af webtilgængelighedsloven og relevante krav i EN 301 549. Verificér den gældende version, anvendelsesområdet og krav til tilgængelighedserklæring hos Digitaliseringsstyrelsen. WCAG er en vigtig del af teknisk afprøvning, men en automatisk scanning omfatter kun en del af kravene.

Et praktisk designmål er et brugbart forløb med:

- Tilstrækkelig kontrast i faktisk tekst, knapper, fokus og tilstande.
- Tastaturbetjening, synligt logisk fokus og navngivne dialoger.
- Synlige labels, tilknyttede fejl, semantiske overskrifter og status med andet end farve.
- Smalle skærme, 200 % zoom og tekstforstørrelse uden tab af indhold.
- Reduceret bevægelse og ingen skadeligt blinkende effekter.
- Manuelle prøver med relevante hjælpemidler og brugere.

Kør lokale godkendte automatiske værktøjer i begge temaer og relevante tilstande, men skeln deres fund fra manuelle prøver og organisatorisk accept. En manglende scanner tæller ikke som bestået. Brug ikke “WCAG-kompatibel” eller “tilgængelig” uden den nødvendige bredere vurdering.

## Det Fælles Designsystem

Afklar brug af Det Fælles Designsystem ved borger-/virksomhedsselvbetjening, især i sammenhæng med borger.dk eller virk.dk. Organisationens egne interne værktøjer kan følge dens identitet. Vælg et eksisterende godkendt tema og undgå at et andet UI-bibliotek overskriver det utilsigtet. Hent eller installer ikke biblioteker automatisk.

## Data og sikkerhed i brugerfladen

- Minimer data i appen. Ingen hemmeligheder i frontend, URL’er, generelle logs eller fejlmeddelelser.
- Selvhost godkendte fonte, ikoner og scripts. Eksterne ressourcer og embeds giver netværkskontakt; organisationens tilladelser og behandlingsgrundlag skal være afklaret.
- Brug kun nødvendigt lokalt lager til fx tema og kladder, og afklar datatyper, levetid og sletning. Et temaønske giver ikke tilladelse til tracking.
- Login og roller skal følge organisationens godkendte identitetsløsning, når det kræves. Design ikke en demo, som kan forveksles med en rigtig myndigheds login, betaling eller MitID.
- AI-destination og datadeling er særskilte valg. En EU-model, et lokalt brand eller en privacytekst er ikke i sig selv en databehandleraftale eller fuld isolation.
- Screenshots og afledte rapporter omfattes også af dataregler. Afprøv med tydeligt syntetiske data.

## Rettigheder og licens

Kildens `aura-design` er deklareret EUPL-1.2. Det bestemmer ikke automatisk licensen for et vilkårligt brugerprojekt. Bevar relevante licenser og attribution for materiale, som faktisk genbruges; afklar projektets udgivelseslicens særskilt. Fonte, ikoner og logoer kan have andre vilkår. Et logo/byvåben skal anvendes med rettigheder og efter organisationens regler.

## Kilder til efterfølgende verificering

Links er referencer, ikke automatisk autorisation til netværk eller installation:

- Digitaliseringsstyrelsen: https://digst.dk/ og organisationens egne tilgængelighedsvejledninger.
- W3C WCAG: https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/
- WCAG 2.1, dansk oversættelse fra kilden: https://www.w3.org/Translations/WCAG21-da-20191211/
- Det Fælles Designsystem: https://designsystem.dk/
- Officiel EUPL-information: https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/collection/eupl

# Tokens og temaer

## Tre lag

1. **Brandinput:** organisationens farver, fontfamilier og radius fra det godkendte brandkort.
2. **Semantiske tokens:** `--bg`, `--surface`, `--surface-2`, `--line`, `--ink`, `--muted`, `--primary`, `--primary-text`, `--text-on-primary`, `--accent`, `--focus`, `--ok`, `--warn`, `--danger` og afstands-/typografiskala.
3. **Komponenter:** bruger tokenværdier frem for gentagne brandfarver i CSS.

Ét nyt brand bør i videst muligt omfang ændre tokenlaget frem for hver komponent. Undtagelser skal beskrives. Eksisterende brugeraccept og projektets designsystem går forud for starteren.

## Farve og tekst er forskellige roller

- Bevar den valgte brandfarve som `--primary` i lyst tema. En nødvendig mørk variant er en afledt UI-farve, ikke en ændring af logoet.
- Brug `--primary-text` og `--accent-text` til links og aktiv tekst, når brandets rå farve ikke kontrasterer tilstrækkeligt med baggrunden.
- Knapper skal have særskilte tekstfarver: `--text-on-primary`, `--text-on-primary-hover`, `--text-on-accent`, `--text-on-accent-hover`, `--text-on-danger` og `--text-on-danger-hover`. Hvid er ikke automatisk en sikker farve på en rød knap.
- Status skal også have tekst eller ikon. Farve alene er utilstrækkelig.
- Fokusmarkering skal være synlig på den faktisk tilstødende baggrund. Mål den renderede markering; en målt tokenfarve blandet med gennemsigtighed har en anden kontrast.

Offline-generatoren i `token-generator.md` måler kun de kontrastpar, dens rapport nævner. Det omfatter ikke alle komponenter, illustrationer, billeder, transparens, overlays eller tilstande i den færdige app. En rapport er ikke en WCAG-garanti, og reglerne for tilladelig stor tekst kan ikke antages ud fra en brandfarve.

## Mørkt tema

Afled rolige mørke flader frem for at invertere hele siden. Giv `body` eksplicit baggrund og tekstfarve. Respektér et gemt brugervalg og brug systemtema som neutral fallback i nye apps, medmindre brugeren har valgt en anden standard. Dette ændrer ikke værtsappen Auras eksisterende tema eller brugerindstillinger.

```css
:root { color-scheme: light dark; }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root:not([data-theme="light"]) { /* De godkendte mørke tokens */ }
}
:root[data-theme="dark"] { color-scheme: dark; }
:root[data-theme="light"] { color-scheme: light; }
```

Et farvet headerbånd skal også have målt tekstkontrast i begge temaer. Lad ikke almindelige navigationslabels arve en undtagelse for stor tekst. En negativ logoversion vælges med en lokal godkendt fil; flerfarvede logoer inverteres ikke.

## Typografi, afstand og bevægelse

- Brug højst én brødtekstfamilie og én evt. displayfamilie; mono er en særskilt rolle til kode/tal.
- Brødtekst typisk mindst 16 px, læselig linjeafstand og omkring 68 tegn pr. linje. `clamp()` kan skalere overskrifter, men må ikke forhindre zoom.
- Tal, som skal sammenlignes, får `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` og dansk `Intl`-format, når målgruppen er dansk.
- Brug en sammenhængende afstandsskala, fx 4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64 px, og følg organisationens radius i stedet for tilfældige afrundinger.
- Sigt efter generøse klikflader, fx 44 px. Den konkrete tilgængelighedsvurdering skal også omfatte afstand og alternative handlinger.
- Hold animationer korte og funktionelle. Slå dekorativ bevægelse fra ved `prefers-reduced-motion`; bevar information om fokus, valgt tilstand og igangværende arbejde.

## Ændringer i tokens

Valider farver, fontnavne og præcis tre ikke-negative radiusværdier, før kode genereres. Interpolér ikke usanitiseret sideindhold i CSS. Gem både input og den faktiske kontrastoversigt lokalt under projektets dataregler. Lad ikke automatiske brandgæt eller en generator erstatte brugerens godkendelse af designet.

Skill: Design og byg gennemarbejdede webapps og hjemmesider

## Formål

Skab visuelt sammenhængende, brugervenlige og teknisk velfungerende
webapps og hjemmesider.

Resultatet skal opleves som et færdigt produkt med en bevidst
designretning – ikke som en generisk skabelon.

Design skal understøtte indholdet, målgruppen og brugerens vigtigste
handlinger. Æstetik må aldrig stå i vejen for forståelse eller funktion.


## 1. Forstå opgaven før du designer

Identificér:

- Hvad er produktets formål?
- Hvem er målgruppen?
- Hvilken opgave skal brugeren først og fremmest kunne løse?
- Hvad er sidens eller appens primære handling?
- Er løsningen offentlig, intern, kommerciel eller personlig?
- Findes der allerede en visuel identitet?
- Er der særlige krav til tilgængelighed, sprog eller databeskyttelse?

Undersøg eksisterende kode og relevante materialer, før du ændrer noget.

Hvis information mangler:
- Vælg fornuftige standarder ved mindre designbeslutninger.
- Stil kun spørgsmål, når svaret væsentligt påvirker funktion,
  informationsarkitektur eller brand.
- Forklar kort væsentlige antagelser.
- Opfind ikke officielle oplysninger, kundeudtalelser eller integrationer.

Tilpas ambitionsniveauet til opgaven. En enkel side skal ikke gøres
unødigt kompleks.


## 2. Vælg en tydelig designretning

Definér designretningen, før komponenterne bygges.

Beskriv den med 3–5 egenskaber, eksempelvis:

- Rolig, troværdig, lokal og imødekommende.
- Præcis, professionel, kompakt og effektiv.
- Redaktionel, varm, karakterfuld og indholdsrig.
- Enkel, teknisk, moderne og fokuseret.

Vælg én sammenhængende retning frem for at blande mange stilarter.

Tilpas designet til produktet:
- Offentlige løsninger: forståelighed, tryghed og tilgængelighed.
- Arbejdsværktøjer: overblik, effektivitet og tydelige tilstande.
- Marketinghjemmesider: fortælling, troværdighed og næste handling.
- Kreative porteføljer: særpræg, billeder og typografisk karakter.
- E-handel: produktforståelse, sammenligning og tryg købsproces.

Brug ikke automatisk den samme skrifttype, farvepalet og kortstruktur
til alle projekter.


## 3. Respektér brand og kilder

Hvis en designguide findes:
- Følg dens farver, typografi, logoanvendelse og øvrige regler.
- Skeln mellem bindende regler og inspiration.
- Brug de leverede aktiver frem for hjemmelavede efterligninger.

Hvis en designguide ikke findes:
- Skab et konsistent, selvstændigt designforslag.
- Beskriv det som et forslag, ikke som en officiel identitet.
- Efterlign ikke officielle logoer eller mærker på en måde, der kan
  give indtryk af godkendelse eller tilknytning.

Brug kun billeder, skrifter og andre aktiver, som projektet må anvende.
Indlæs ikke eksterne ressourcer uden at kontrollere projektets rammer.


## 4. Byg et lille designsystem

Definér fælles designværdier, før siderne detaljeres.

### Farver

Opret semantiske farver til:
- Sidens baggrund.
- Primære og sekundære overflader.
- Primær og afdæmpet tekst.
- Kantlinjer.
- Primær handling.
- Accent.
- Succes, advarsel og fejl.

Brug få farver med tydelige roller.

En mulig startpalette til et roligt, grønt design:
- Baggrund: #FAFBF8
- Overflade: #FFFFFF
- Afdæmpet overflade: #EDF2E9
- Primær tekst: #243F39
- Primær handling: #3E6049
- Kantlinje: #DFE5DB

Paletten er kun et eksempel. Kontrollér kontrast i den faktiske
anvendelse, og justér især sekundær tekst efter behov.

Brug ikke farve som eneste signal for betydning.

### Typografi

- Vælg én primær skrifttype og eventuelt én supplerende.
- Brug skrifter, som allerede er tilgængelige, når det er muligt.
- Skab karakter gennem hierarki, vægt og proportioner – ikke ved at
  bruge mange forskellige skrifttyper.
- Brug som udgangspunkt 16 px til almindelig brødtekst.
- Brug mindre tekst med omtanke og ikke til afgørende information.
- Giv brødtekst en linjehøjde omkring 1,5–1,7.
- Hold længere tekstblokke omkring 45–75 tegn pr. linje.
- Brug flydende overskriftsstørrelser, hvor det giver mening.

Overskrifter skal have en tydelig relation til hinanden.
Spring ikke tilfældigt mellem størrelser og vægte.

### Afstande

Brug en konsistent afstandsskala, eksempelvis:
4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 og 96 px.

Afstande skal vise sammenhæng:
- Lille afstand mellem elementer, der hører sammen.
- Større afstand mellem forskellige grupper.
- Mest luft mellem hovedsektioner.

### Former og dybde

- Vælg en konsekvent strategi for hjørner.
- Brug kantlinjer til diskret struktur.
- Brug kun skygger, når de hjælper med at vise lag eller interaktion.
- Undgå at give alle elementer samme kortbaggrund og skygge.

### Design tokens

Saml gentagne værdier i CSS-variabler eller projektets eksisterende
tokensystem.

Eksempel:

:root {
  --color-bg: #fafbf8;
  --color-surface: #ffffff;
  --color-text: #243f39;
  --color-primary: #3e6049;
  --color-border: #dfe5db;

  --radius-control: 6px;
  --radius-panel: 12px;

  --space-1: 4px;
  --space-2: 8px;
  --space-3: 12px;
  --space-4: 16px;
  --space-6: 24px;
  --space-8: 32px;
  --space-12: 48px;
}


## 5. Planlæg informationsarkitekturen

Organisér indhold efter brugerens behov, ikke efter organisationens
interne struktur.

Gør det hurtigt at forstå:
1. Hvad er dette?
2. Hvad kan jeg gøre her?
3. Hvad er vigtigst for mig?
4. Hvad skal jeg gøre nu?

Brug få, tydelige navigationspunkter.
Vis aktiv placering.
Brug velkendte betegnelser frem for kreative, men uklare navne.

### For hjemmesider

En mulig struktur:
- Header med identitet og navigation.
- Introduktion med klart værdiløfte.
- Primær handling.
- Relevant indhold, produkter eller ydelser.
- Dokumentation eller troværdighedsskabende information.
- Næste skridt.
- Footer med relevante oplysninger.

Brug kun sektioner, som har et reelt formål.
Opfind ikke kundeudtalelser, referencer eller resultater.

### For webapps

En mulig struktur:
- Navigation og aktuel placering.
- Sidetitel og kort forklaring.
- Primær handling.
- Søgning, filtre eller relevante værktøjer.
- Arbejdsområde, liste, tabel eller detaljevisning.
- Tydelig feedback og næste skridt.

En webapp behøver ikke en stor marketing-introduktion.
Prioritér arbejdsområdet, når brugeren kommer for at løse en opgave.


## 6. Skab visuel prioritering

Hver skærm skal have et tydeligt fokus.

- Giv den vigtigste handling størst visuel vægt.
- Brug sekundære handlinger mere afdæmpet.
- Brug tekstlinks til mindre vigtige handlinger.
- Giv destruktive handlinger et tydeligt, men afbalanceret udtryk.
- Lad ikke alle elementer konkurrere om opmærksomheden.

Brug variation i:
- Størrelse.
- Typografisk vægt.
- Kontrast.
- Placering.
- Afstand.
- Overflade.

Undgå at fremhæve alt med stærke farver, fed tekst og store knapper.


## 7. Design komponenter til deres indhold

Vælg komponent efter opgaven:

- Kort til selvstændige indholdsenheder.
- Tabeller til sammenligning og strukturerede data.
- Lister til gentagne, let skannede elementer.
- Faner til nært beslægtede visninger.
- Dialoger til afgrænsede opgaver.
- Separate sider til længere eller komplekse forløb.

Brug ikke kort til alt.

### Knapper
- Brug handlingsorienterede tekster.
- Skriv eksempelvis “Gem ændringer” frem for “OK”.
- Brug ens højde, afstande og ikonplacering.
- Vis tydelige hover-, fokus-, deaktiveret- og indlæsningstilstande.
- Undgå ikonknapper uden tilgængeligt navn.

### Formularer
- Brug synlige labels.
- Brug ikke placeholdertekst som eneste label.
- Angiv korrekt inputtype og autocomplete.
- Spørg kun om nødvendige oplysninger.
- Vis krav og validering tæt på det relevante felt.
- Bevar indtastede værdier ved fejl.
- Forklar, hvad der sker efter indsendelse.
- Undgå at vise succes, før handlingen er gennemført.

### Søgning og filtre
- Brug tydelige labels.
- Vis, når et filter er aktivt.
- Vis resultatantal, når det hjælper.
- Giv mulighed for at nulstille filtreringen.
- Forklar tomme søgeresultater.

### Dialoger
- Giv dialogen en tydelig titel.
- Håndtér fokus korrekt.
- Giv en forståelig lukkemulighed.
- Understøt Escape, når handlingen kan afbrydes.
- Returnér fokus til det udløsende element efter lukning.
- Forebyg utilsigtet tab af indhold ved vigtige handlinger.


## 8. Design alle relevante tilstande

En funktion er ikke færdig, når kun normaltilstanden er designet.

Håndtér efter behov:
- Indlæsning.
- Tom tilstand.
- Ingen søgeresultater.
- Succes.
- Valideringsfejl.
- Netværks- eller serverfejl.
- Manglende adgang.
- Deaktiveret handling.
- Langsom forbindelse.
- Delvist tilgængelige data.

Giv altid en brugbar forklaring og et muligt næste skridt.

Indlæsning må ikke ligne et tomt resultat.
En fejl må ikke præsenteres som en succes.
Eksempeldata må ikke fremstå som rigtige data.


## 9. Skriv præcis og menneskelig mikrocopy

Brug målgruppens sprog.

Skriv:
- Kort.
- Konkret.
- Venligt.
- Handlingsorienteret.
- Uden unødvendig jargon.

Forklar handlingens resultat:
- “Tilmeld dig mødet”
- “Download rapport”
- “Gem ændringer”
- “Prøv igen”
- “Nulstil filtre”

Fejlbeskeder skal forklare:
1. Hvad gik galt?
2. Er brugerens arbejde bevaret?
3. Hvad kan brugeren gøre nu?

Undgå:
- Uklare “Der opstod en fejl”-beskeder uden næste skridt.
- Overdrevet begejstring ved almindelige handlinger.
- Skyldplacering hos brugeren.
- Påstande, som systemet ikke kan dokumentere.


## 10. Gør designet responsivt

Design til indhold og tilgængelig plads – ikke kun til bestemte enheder.

- Brug fleksible grids og layouts.
- Undgå vandret rulning på almindelige sider.
- Tilpas navigation, kort og værktøjslinjer på små skærme.
- Lad formularer bruge den tilgængelige bredde.
- Hold primære handlinger lette at finde.
- Bevar vigtigt indhold på mobil.
- Brug passende klik- og trykflader.
- Sigt efter cirka 44 × 44 px for centrale touch-kontroller.

Test mindst:
- Smal mobil.
- Bred mobil eller tablet.
- Almindelig desktop.
- Stor desktop.

Kontrollér også:
- Lange overskrifter.
- Lange navne og labels.
- Mange listeelementer.
- Forstørret tekst.
- Både meget lidt og meget indhold.


## 11. Prioritér tilgængelighed

Sigt efter WCAG 2.2 niveau AA, hvor det er relevant.

- Brug semantisk HTML.
- Brug rigtige knapper til handlinger og links til navigation.
- Sørg for logisk overskriftshierarki.
- Giv formularfelter tilknyttede labels.
- Sørg for fuld tastaturbetjening.
- Vis tydelig fokusmarkering.
- Skab en logisk fokusrækkefølge.
- Brug tilstrækkelig tekstkontrast.
- Giv meningsfulde billeder alternativ tekst.
- Skjul dekorative ikoner for skærmlæsere.
- Gør vigtige statusændringer tilgængelige for hjælpemidler.
- Respektér brugerens ønske om reduceret bevægelse.

Som udgangspunkt:
- Mindst 4,5:1 kontrast for almindelig tekst.
- Mindst 3:1 for stor tekst.
- Relevante kontrolgrænser og fokusmarkeringer skal være tydelige.

Påstå ikke fuld tilgængelighed alene på baggrund af en visuel kontrol.


## 12. Brug billeder, illustrationer og ikoner bevidst

Visuelle elementer skal:
- Forklare.
- Understøtte identiteten.
- Skabe relevant stemning.
- Hjælpe med orientering.

De skal ikke blot udfylde tom plads.

- Brug en sammenhængende ikonstil.
- Kombinér uklare ikoner med tekst.
- Bevar billeders proportioner.
- Brug korrekt beskæring.
- Angiv dimensioner, når det kan forebygge layoutskift.
- Optimér tunge aktiver.
- Brug enkel original grafik, når det passer bedre end stockfotos.

Undgå dekorative illustrationer, som konkurrerer med hovedopgaven.


## 13. Brug bevægelse med tilbageholdenhed

Animation skal forklare ændringer og give feedback.

- Brug korte, rolige overgange.
- Animér især opacity og transform.
- Undgå bevægelse, der forsinker brugerens arbejde.
- Undgå konstant animation uden et tydeligt formål.
- Understøt prefers-reduced-motion.

Hovereffekter må ikke være den eneste måde at opdage funktioner på.


## 14. Implementér i projektets eksisterende rammer

- Undersøg det eksisterende framework og komponentmønster.
- Bevar fungerende arkitektur og afhængigheder.
- Genbrug eksisterende komponenter, når de passer.
- Tilføj kun nye afhængigheder, når de giver reel værdi.
- Følg miljøets regler for installation, data og integrationer.
- Adskil gentaget UI i passende komponenter.
- Brug læsbare navne og overskuelig tilstandshåndtering.
- Undgå unødvendige abstraktioner.

Byg reel funktionalitet:
- Knapper skal udføre deres angivne handling.
- Filtre skal filtrere.
- Formularer skal validere.
- Gemte ændringer skal håndteres korrekt.
- Fejl skal vises forståeligt.

Hvis en integration mangler:
- Forklar begrænsningen.
- Markér eventuelle eksempler.
- Simulér ikke en vellykket virkelig handling.


## 15. Behandl data med omtanke

- Indsaml kun nødvendige oplysninger.
- Vælg datalagring efter, hvem der må læse og skrive.
- Skeln mellem personlige, fælles og offentlige oplysninger.
- Undgå persondata i eksempelindhold.
- Gem aldrig adgangskoder eller hemmeligheder i frontendkode.
- Forklar væsentlige konsekvenser ved indsendelse.
- Stol ikke på skjult UI som adgangskontrol.
- Håndhæv adgang gennem den tilgængelige backend.

Brug ikke juridiske løfter som “fuldt GDPR-sikker” uden et
dokumenteret grundlag.


## 16. Kontrollér resultatet visuelt og funktionelt

Se den faktisk renderede løsning. Stol ikke kun på koden.

Kontrollér:
- Er sidens formål tydeligt?
- Er den vigtigste handling let at finde?
- Er typografihierarkiet sammenhængende?
- Er der passende luft?
- Er sekundær tekst læsbar?
- Er elementer korrekt justeret?
- Er der overlap, afskæring eller vandret overflow?
- Fungerer navigation, formularer og filtre?
- Er indlæsning, fejl og tomme tilstande håndteret?
- Er der runtimefejl?
- Fungerer mobilvisningen?
- Kan de vigtigste opgaver udføres med tastatur?

Ret konkrete problemer og kontrollér igen.

Skeln mellem:
- Visuelt kontrolleret.
- Funktionelt afprøvet.
- Testet med rigtige integrationer.

Påstå ikke test, som ikke er udført.


## 17. Undgå generiske designfælder

Undgå som automatisk standard:
- Store gradientoverskrifter.
- Tilfældige lilla eller blå accenter.
- Glaseffekter på alle flader.
- Identiske kort i alle sektioner.
- Overdrevne skygger.
- Meget store hjørner på alle elementer.
- Små, lysegrå tekster med dårlig læsbarhed.
- Overflødige badges og ikoner.
- Store introduktionsfelter i effektivitetsorienterede apps.
- Falske tal, kundeudsagn eller aktivitetsindikatorer.
- Dekorative knapper, som ikke virker.

Disse virkemidler er ikke forbudte, men skal vælges bevidst,
fordi de passer til produktet.


## 18. Afslut med en kort og ærlig overlevering

Fortæl:
- Hvad der er bygget eller ændret.
- Hvilke hovedfunktioner der findes.
- Hvad der er testet.
- Om data er eksempler.
- Om noget kræver opsætning eller yderligere arbejde.

Hold forklaringen kort, medmindre brugeren ønsker dokumentation.

Et flot udtryk er ikke nok. Løsningen skal være forståelig,
funktionel, tilgængelig og ærlig om sine begrænsninger.


## Opgaveskabelon

Når dette skill bruges, udfyld:

**Produkt:**
[Hvad skal bygges?]

**Målgruppe:**
[Hvem skal bruge det?]

**Primær opgave:**
[Hvad skal brugeren først og fremmest kunne gøre?]

**Vigtigste sider eller visninger:**
[Liste]

**Designretning:**
[3–5 egenskaber]

**Brandmateriale:**
[Designguide, logo, farver, skrifter – eller intet eksisterende]

**Indhold og data:**
[Rigtige data, leveret indhold eller tydeligt markerede eksempler]

**Funktioner og integrationer:**
[Hvad skal virke?]

**Tekniske rammer:**
[Eksisterende projekt, framework og begrænsninger]

**Særlige krav:**
[Sprog, tilgængelighed, adgang, mobil, databeskyttelse]

Start derefter med at undersøge projektet, vælg en tydelig
designretning, implementér løsningen og kontrollér resultatet.

skills.summary: GradientDecks designbedømmelse til en ny visuel retning og en kritisk kvalitetsgennemgang af brugerflader. Aktiveres pr. besked med /design og supplerer den altid-aktive designhjælp.

faq.hvad: Vælger og gennemfører én visuel retning til nyt arbejde med GradientDecks metode: en række konkrete verdener at bygge i, konsekvent typografi, farve og komposition, og en kritisk gennemgang af det renderede resultat. Aktiveres pr. besked med /design oven på den altid-aktive designhjælp og ændrer ikke grundmetoden, planer eller godkendelser.
faq.hvornaar: Når et nyt produkt eller en ny side skal have en egen visuel retning, før koden skrives, eller når en færdig brugerflade skal kritisk gennemgås, poleres eller gøres mindre generisk.
faq.resultat: En gennemført retning med planfil i .gradientdeck/pages/, et første udkast bygget konsekvent i retningen og en kort gennemgang af fundne og rettede problemer. Retningen trækkes af et script, der kræver kommandogodkendelse; uden godkendelse vælges retningen i teksten i stedet.
faq.ikke: Den erstatter ikke Auras grundmetode og designhjælp, godkender ingen planer og giver ingen fil-, kommando- eller netværkstilladelser. Den henter aldrig billeder eller stile fra nettet uden egen godkendelse.

# GradientDeck · harness-design

You are a design director who also writes the code, and the bar is work people remember: a clear point of view, made for this product, finished to the last detail. Left alone, your output is the safe average of every site you learned from. This skill exists to pull you off that average. Go all the way with the idea you choose, author everything the page needs at full quality, and know why each choice fits this product. A good result is one an unrelated product could not use unchanged, and one the user would be proud to ship today.

## Aura Prime

This skill runs inside Aura. The design help is always active and remains the main build method; this skill is a per-message complement (the `/design` token activates it for that send). It never changes the ground rules, the build method, plans, approvals or data rules, and it grants no tool, file or network permission.

- **Inspiration, not imitation.** The worlds describe real materials, places and systems. Use their discipline for structure, type, color and detail. Never imitate another product, and never put logos, brand names, trademarks or real product names in the output — a design that reads as a specific existing product has failed.
- **The roll needs command approval.** `scripts/roll.mjs` is a Node script. Running it is a command and requires Aura's command approval. If approval is denied, do not run it: read `worlds/worlds.json` as plain text, deal the worlds honestly yourself (no cherry-picking toward a look already decided), write the plan file yourself, and do the roll's `check` yourself from the rendered page. Say you rolled by hand. If Node is not available, follow the without-Node rule in `references/direction.md` instead: build your third-ranked candidate with no dealt worlds, write the plan file yourself, and say so. Either way the roll's rules stay binding.
- **Photographs are references, not downloads.** `photos/photos.json` lists openly licensed Wikimedia Commons photographs with external URLs, authors and licences. The URLs are data; fetching anything from the network needs its own approval. A page that uses them credits each author and licence.
- **Licence and attribution.** Ported from github.com/VenoM9078/gradientdeck-skill (MIT). The licence is preserved as `LICENSE` next to this file. The method and data are used under MIT; what you build belongs to the user's project.

## Setup

1. Read this file fully and answer the three questions in section 1.
2. Load the playbook for the job: in New world, `references/direction.md`, and run the roll it describes before any code; in Extend or New surface, `references/extend.md`; for a named command, its file in section 4.
3. Immediately before writing or editing any UI code, read `references/craft.md`, even for a small change. It holds the floor for type, color, space, finish and the generic defaults to refuse. Skip it only for planning or review with no edits.

Open other reference files only for the primitive you're deciding (section 5).

## 1. Read the situation before anything else

Answer these three questions in order. They decide everything that follows.

**Situation: how much may you invent?**

| Situation | When | What you do |
|---|---|---|
| **Extend** | The codebase already has UI, and you're adding or changing a page or component in that look | Inherit everything. No new direction. Load `references/extend.md` |
| **New surface** | The codebase has a look, but this is a new kind of page (first pricing page, first docs) | Inherit tokens and components. Decide structure only. Load `references/extend.md`, then `references/composition.md` |
| **New world** | Greenfield, or the user asked for a redesign | Choose a direction before any code: write candidates, run the roll, fill the plan file it saves. Load `references/direction.md` first; this is not optional |

If you can't tell, look: a `DESIGN.md`, a Tailwind `@theme`, CSS custom properties, a component folder, or existing pages mean Extend or New surface. When in doubt, ask one question rather than guess.

**Mode: what does success look like on this surface?**

| Mode | Surfaces | Success | Where character lives |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Persuade** | Landing, marketing, launch, portfolio | The visitor gets the offer, wants it and acts. Here the design is the product | Everywhere: one idea owns structure, type, color, imagery and motion |
| **Operate** | App screens, dashboards, settings, admin, tools | The task gets done fast and without doubt, every day | In precise details: type, palette, density, states and one signature, never in invented layouts or controls |
| **Read** | Docs, articles, blogs, legal | The reader understands, and the reading is worth staying for | In the frame, headings and imagery around a calm column |

Pick the mode from the surface being built, not from the product. A developer tool's landing page is Persuade; its settings page is Operate. A product that spans modes gets one direction that steps down from Persuade to Read to Operate.

**Inputs: what is already decided?** Check, in this order, and treat each as authority over your own taste:
1. What the user said in this conversation.
2. `DESIGN.md`, `.gradientdeck/decisions.md` and the page's plan in `.gradientdeck/pages/`, if present.
3. The existing code: tokens, components, the closest existing page.
4. Brand assets the user provided.

Your taste fills only the gaps these leave.

## 2. Work in this order

1. **Note.** Before writing code, write a short note (3–5 lines) in your reply: situation, mode, what you're inheriting, the conventions you'll follow, and the one thing you'll make specific to this product. In Extend and New surface, the note is the pre-flight contract in `references/extend.md`. In New world, it is the plan file the roll saves, filled in.
2. **Draft.** Read `references/craft.md`, then build the whole thing. Every section the page needs ships complete: write the copy (`references/copy.md`), author the demo content, place the photographs, build the signature moment. Reuse existing components before writing new ones.
3. **Taste-test.** Always do this, then write it in your reply as a short `Review:` list of what you found and fixed. If a browser tool is available, render at 1440, 768 and 390 pixels and look; if not, read your markup and styles as a renderer would. Check:
    - **Job:** the main action is obvious and working on the first screen.
    - **Layout:** one container width and shared edges; related things sit closer than unrelated ones; gaps come from one scale; nothing floats unanchored or crowds an edge.
    - **Proportion and pace:** headings suit their content; columns balance; sections vary in density and shape, and the page ends on a real close.
    - **Specific:** something on the page could only belong to this product.
    - **Finished and honest:** no invented claims, no placeholders, no broken strings, nothing stuck open; demo content labelled.
    - **Floor:** contrast, visible focus, and the 390px layout holds.
    For each failure, open the reference for that primitive (`references/space-and-layout.md`, `references/typography.md`, `references/composition.md`, `references/tells.md`, `references/direction.md` if it reads generic or timid) and fix it. In New world, also run the roll's `check` command and answer its lines from the screenshots.
4. **Fresh eyes.** If you can start a subagent, give a fresh reviewer the request, the plan file, the three screenshots and `references/review.md`, none of your reasoning, and fix its P0 and P1 findings. A reviewer who didn't build the page sees what you stopped seeing. If you can't, reread the screenshots as a stranger would.
5. **Fix and stop.** After the last fix, render all three widths again. **Stop after two rounds** of test-and-fix; report anything left over rather than looping.
6. **Record.** Write `DESIGN.md` when you're setting up a product's system (several pages, or the user asked). For any decision that should hold next time, add a dated line to `.gradientdeck/decisions.md`. Never put design notes, scores or signatures in the product's code or comments.

## 3. The floor under every page

- **NEVER invent claims.** No made-up metrics, customer logos, testimonials, ratings, user counts, press quotes, awards, prices, integrations or dates. If the page needs proof the user hasn't given, choose a structure that doesn't depend on it, and write around a missing fact ("Spring dates go out by email first").
- **MUST author demonstration content.** A demo's entries, sample names, example data and drawings are design material, not claims: make them at full quality and label them as an example where a visitor could take them as real. A section is never dropped for lack of supplied content. List every example in your report so the user can replace it.
- **MUST ship a page that reads finished.** No bracketed placeholders, "TBD" or lorem ipsum in visible text. Honesty is not austerity.
- **MUST meet the accessibility floor.** Text contrast of at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for text 24px and up, or 19px up when bold). Visible focus on every interactive element. Every animation has a reduced-motion version. Interactive targets of at least 24×24px, and 44×44px on touch surfaces. Meaning is never carried by color alone.
- **MUST use the system.** Every color, font, size, radius, shadow and spacing value references a token. Add a new value to the tokens on purpose; never inline a one-off.
- **SHOULD keep the structure people expect in Operate and Read**, and in Extend and New surface. A shop has product cards, docs have a sidebar, a settings page has the usual controls.
- **MUST commit in New world Persuade work.** Build the direction you chose at page scale, not a softened reading of it (`references/direction.md`). Usability and the floor still win any conflict.
- **SHOULD use the project's icon set** if it has one; never emoji or Unicode symbols as icons (`references/imagery.md`).
- **AVOID the generic defaults** in `references/tells.md` and drawn fake environments (browser bars, traffic-light dots, phone frames). The product's own interface built in HTML, or a terminal with the real commands, is content, not costume.

## 4. Commands

The user may name one of these. If they don't, infer it from the request.

| Command | Job | Load |
|---|---|---|
| `build` (default) | Make or change UI, following situation and mode | depends on situation |
| `direction` | Choose a visual direction for new work | `references/direction.md` |
| `reroll` | New direction for a New world page: `reroll bolder`, `reroll safer`, or `reroll standard` | `references/direction.md` |
| `extract` | Read an existing codebase's design system into `DESIGN.md` | `references/extend.md`, `references/design-md.md` |
| `review` | Critique a page or component; findings with severity | `references/review.md`, `references/tells.md`, plus the primitives the findings touch |
| `polish` | Final craft pass on finished UI | `references/polish.md` |
| `deslop` | Remove generic defaults from the current change only | `references/tells.md` |
| `bolder` / `quieter` | Increase or reduce expression by one step | `references/principles.md` |
| `simplify` | Remove elements until each remaining one earns its place | `references/principles.md` |
| `retype` / `recolor` / `reflow` | Rework one primitive, keep the rest | that primitive's file |
| `animate` | Add or fix motion with purpose | `references/motion.md` |

## 5. Load what you touch

| You are deciding... | Load |
|---|---|
| The quality floor, before any UI code | `references/craft.md` |
| Core judgment, steering verbs | `references/principles.md` |
| Fonts, sizes, weights, line length | `references/typography.md` |
| Palette, contrast, light/dark, gradients | `references/color.md` |
| Spacing, grids, density, alignment, radius, elevation | `references/space-and-layout.md` |
| Page structure, sections, first viewport, navigation | `references/composition.md` |
| Animation, transitions, hover | `references/motion.md` |
| States, forms, feedback, focus, small craft details | `references/interaction.md` |
| Photos, illustration, icons, logos | `references/imagery.md` |
| Headlines, buttons, errors, microcopy | `references/copy.md` |
| Tables, filters, dashboards, data, app chrome | `references/apps-and-data.md` |
| Mobile and breakpoints | `references/responsive.md` |
| Accessibility beyond the floor | `references/accessibility.md` |
| What reads as generic, and what to do instead | `references/tells.md` |
| Greenfield direction | `references/direction.md` |
| Working inside an existing codebase | `references/extend.md` |
| Critique | `references/review.md` |
| Final pass | `references/polish.md` |
| The `DESIGN.md` file format | `references/design-md.md` |

All reference files are in the `references/` folder next to this file. The direction roll is `scripts/roll.mjs`; its worlds are in `worlds/worlds.json` and its photo library in `photos/photos.json` (see Aura Prime: the roll needs command approval, and without approval or Node you deal from `worlds/worlds.json` as plain text yourself).

## 6. Reporting back

End every design task with: what you built, which decisions you made and why (two or three lines), anything you couldn't verify, the facts you wrote around, and every piece of example content you authored, so the user can supply the real thing. Keep it short. Don't grade your own work with scores. In New world, close with one line offering a bolder or safer re-roll (`references/direction.md`).

# Accessibility

The floor in SKILL.md (contrast, visible focus, reduced motion, target size, color never alone) is the minimum. This file is how to build so the whole interface works with a keyboard, a screen reader, zoom, high-contrast modes and reduced motion. Accessibility rules are `MUST` and `NEVER` in every mode. Criteria numbers refer to WCAG 2.2.

## Decide

1. **What is each element, semantically?** A button, a link, a heading, a list, a form field. Choose the native element first; style it second.
2. **How does a keyboard user move through this?** Walk the tab order before styling focus.
3. **What changes without a page load?** Each async update, error and dialog needs focus or announcement handling.

## Rules

### Semantic HTML first

- MUST use landmarks: one `<main>`, plus `<header>`, `<nav>`, `<footer>`, `<aside>` where they apply. Label multiple navs (`aria-label="Primary"`).
- MUST have one `<h1>` per page and headings in order without skipped levels. Heading level follows structure, not font size; style any level to look as needed.
- Buttons do things (`<button>`); links go places (`<a href>`). NEVER put a click handler on a `<div>` or `<span>`. An `<a>` without `href` is not focusable.
- Lists of things are `<ul>`/`<ol>`; tabular data is a `<table>` with `<th scope>` and a caption or accessible name (1.3.1).
- Set `lang` on `<html>` (3.1.1) and on passages in another language (3.1.2).
- DOM order MUST match visual reading order (1.3.2, 2.4.3). Don't rearrange with CSS `order`, grid placement or absolute positioning in a way that changes meaning.

### Keyboard

- Everything operable by pointer MUST be operable by keyboard (2.1.1), with no keyboard traps (2.1.2).
- Tab order follows reading order. Don't use positive `tabindex`; use `tabindex="0"` only to make custom widgets focusable and `-1` for elements you focus by script.
- Focus MUST be visible (2.4.7) and not hidden behind sticky headers or footers (2.4.11). Style with `:focus-visible`; the indicator needs 3:1 contrast against its surroundings and should be at least a 2px outline. Never remove outlines without a replacement.
- Content-heavy pages and pages with long nav SHOULD have a skip link to `<main>` as the first focusable element, visible on focus (2.4.1).
- Composite widgets (tabs, menus, listboxes, grids) use one tab stop and arrow keys inside, following established keyboard patterns for that widget.
- Dragging MUST have a single-pointer alternative, such as move buttons or a menu (2.5.7).

### Focus management

- Dialogs: use `<dialog>` with `showModal()` where possible (it makes the page inert and closes on Escape). On open, move focus to the first meaningful control or the dialog heading; keep focus inside while open; on close, return focus to the element that opened it.
- Menus and popovers: Escape closes and returns focus to the trigger. The trigger has `aria-expanded`.
- After deleting an item or changing route in a single-page app, move focus somewhere sensible (the next item, the new page's `<h1>`), never to `<body>`.

### Accessible names

- Every control MUST have an accessible name (4.1.2). Prefer visible text: a `<label for>` for fields, button text for buttons.
- Use `aria-label` only when there is no visible text, such as icon-only buttons (`aria-label="Close"`). Icon-only buttons SHOULD also have a tooltip for sighted users.
- When there is visible text, the accessible name MUST contain it, ideally starting with it (2.5.3), so voice users can say what they see.
- Decorative icons get `aria-hidden="true"`; inline SVGs that convey meaning get a title or name.

### ARIA

- No ARIA is better than bad ARIA. A native element already has the right role, states and keyboard behaviour; use it before adding roles.
- ARIA changes what is announced, not behaviour. If you add `role="button"`, you also owe focusability, Enter and Space handling, and a name.
- Never put `aria-hidden="true"` on anything focusable. Keep states in sync (`aria-expanded`, `aria-selected`, `aria-pressed`, `aria-current`).

### Images and alt text

- Informative images: alt text that says what the image communicates in context, not "image of". Decorative images: `alt=""`.
- Images of text are avoided; when unavoidable, the alt contains the text. Charts need a text summary or a data table.

### Forms

- Every field has a visible, programmatically associated label (3.3.2). Placeholder is not a label.
- Group related controls (radio sets, address blocks) with `<fieldset>` and `<legend>`.
- Errors: identify the field and describe the problem in text (3.3.1) with a suggestion where possible (3.3.3). Link the message with `aria-describedby`, set `aria-invalid="true"` on the field, and on submit move focus to an error summary that links to each field (or to the first invalid field on a short form).
- Use correct `type` and `autocomplete` values so browsers and password managers can fill fields; don't ask for the same information twice in one process (3.3.7). Never block paste into password or code fields (3.3.8).

### Live regions

- Status messages that appear without focus moving (saved, results count, upload progress) MUST be announced (4.1.3): put them in a region with `role="status"` or `aria-live="polite"` that exists in the DOM before the message is inserted.
- Use `role="alert"` (assertive) only for urgent errors. Don't announce every keystroke; debounce.

### Color and contrast

- Text MUST meet the floor: 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text (1.4.3). Check text over images and gradients at the worst point.
- Non-text elements people need to see (field borders, icons that carry meaning, chart marks, focus indicators, control states) MUST have 3:1 against adjacent colors (1.4.11).
- Color MUST NOT be the only signal (1.4.1): errors get an icon and text; links in body text get an underline or another non-color cue.

### Motion and flashing

- Honour `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`: replace movement, parallax and auto-playing animation with fades or no animation (see `motion.md`).
- NEVER flash anything more than three times in any one-second period (2.3.1).
- Auto-moving content that lasts more than five seconds (carousels, tickers) MUST have pause (2.2.2).

### Zoom and reflow

- Text MUST resize to 200% without loss (1.4.4); content MUST reflow at 320 CSS px wide (equivalent to 400% zoom at 1280px) without two-dimensional scrolling, except for content that needs it, such as data tables and maps (1.4.10). Use `rem` for type and avoid fixed heights on text containers.
- Layout MUST survive user text spacing overrides (1.4.12): no clipped text when line height, letter spacing or word spacing increase.
- Hover and focus content (tooltips, popovers) must be dismissible with Escape, hoverable, and stay until dismissed (1.4.13).

### Target size

- Targets MUST be at least 24×24 CSS px, or have enough spacing that a 24px circle on each doesn't overlap another (2.5.8, AA). Inline links in text are exempt. Use 44×44px on touch surfaces (see `responsive.md`).

### Contrast modes

- Respect `forced-colors: active`: don't convey state only with background or box-shadow (they are removed); use borders or outlines, which take system colors. If a custom focus style uses `box-shadow`, add `outline: 2px solid transparent` too; forced-colors mode removes the shadow but paints the outline in a system color.
- Optionally strengthen borders and muted text under `prefers-contrast: more`.

## Generic defaults to catch

- **`outline: none` with no replacement** → keyboard users lose their place → `:focus-visible` style with 3:1 contrast.
- **Div buttons and icon buttons with no name** → silent or unreachable → `<button>` with text or `aria-label`.
- **Light gray placeholder as the only label** → fails contrast and vanishes → visible label.
- **ARIA roles sprinkled on native elements** → redundant or conflicting → remove them.
- **Modal that doesn't trap or return focus** → users tab into the page behind.

## Check

- [ ] Landmarks present; one `<h1>`; headings in order; `lang` set.
- [ ] Every interactive element reachable and operable by Tab, Enter, Space, Escape and arrows where expected.
- [ ] Focus always visible, never hidden under sticky elements.
- [ ] Dialogs move focus in, contain it, close on Escape and return focus.
- [ ] Every control has a name containing its visible label.
- [ ] Field errors are linked with `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`; async status announced politely.
- [ ] Text 4.5:1 (large 3:1); UI parts and focus indicators 3:1; nothing by color alone.
- [ ] Reduced motion honoured; nothing flashes more than three times a second.
- [ ] Page works at 320 CSS px and 200% text; targets ≥24×24px.
- [ ] Visual order matches DOM order.

# Apps and data

Operate mode in depth: app shells, tables, filters, forms, dashboards and settings. Here people come back daily to get work done, so speed, predictability and density beat expression. Personality lives in type, color and one signature detail (see `principles.md`), never in reinvented controls.

## Decide

1. **What are the three most frequent tasks on this screen?** They get the primary positions; everything else goes one level down.
2. **How often, and how expert, are the users?** Daily experts want density and shortcuts; occasional users want labels, space and guidance.
3. **What decision does this data support?** A dashboard or table exists to answer a question. Write the question before choosing a component.
4. **What already exists?** Inherit the shell, table and form patterns of the codebase (see `extend.md`). Never introduce a second table style.

## Rules

### App shell

- SHOULD follow convention: primary navigation in a left sidebar (many sections, or sections that grow) or a top bar (five or fewer stable sections). Account and settings sit at a far end of the nav.
- Every page SHOULD have a header with the page title, an optional one-line context, and the primary action at the end of the header row. One primary action per page; others are secondary or in an overflow menu.
- The current location MUST be indicated by more than color (weight, a marker, `aria-current="page"`).
- Keep the shell stable: nav, header height and action positions don't move between pages.

### Density

- Choose density from task and frequency, not taste: monitoring and bulk editing → compact; occasional review → comfortable. Offer a density toggle only when both audiences really exist.
- Density changes row height and padding, never text below the readable minimum or targets below 24×24px.

### Tables

- Text columns align left; numbers align right with tabular numerals (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`) so digits line up; headers align with their column's content.
- Keep units and precision consistent within a column; put the unit in the header, not in every cell.
- Header row SHOULD be sticky in any table taller than the viewport. The first column (the row's identity) SHOULD be sticky when the table scrolls sideways.
- Row height: around 28–36px compact, 40–48px comfortable (`space-and-layout.md`), taller only when rows hold two lines or avatars. Pick one per table.
- Use either thin dividers or zebra striping, not both. Dividers suit most tables; zebra helps wide tables with many columns where the eye tracks across.
- Truncate long text with an ellipsis only where the full value is available on hover and on keyboard focus (title alone is not keyboard-accessible), or in the row detail. Never truncate numbers, IDs or amounts.
- Sortable headers are buttons with a visible sort indicator on the active column and `aria-sort` on its header cell.
- Selection: a checkbox column with a header checkbox for select-all (with an indeterminate state), and a bulk action bar showing the count ("3 selected") that replaces or sits over the table toolbar.
- Row states: loading uses skeleton rows of the real row height; an empty table shows the empty state inside the table frame (see `copy.md`); a failed load shows the error and a retry in place. Row actions on hover MUST also be reachable by keyboard and on touch.

### Filters and search

- Active filters MUST be visible as removable chips or a summary line, with a "Clear all". A hidden active filter makes the data look wrong.
- Show the result count, and update it as filters change. Show per-option counts when they help people avoid empty results.
- Search SHOULD filter as you type (debounced) for local data; for slow queries, search on Enter and show progress.
- Filter and sort state SHOULD live in the URL so views can be shared and survive reload.

### Forms in apps

- Group related fields under short headings; order them as the user thinks about the task, not as the database stores them.
- Inline edit suits single values edited often (a name, a status). Use a form or panel when several fields must change together or need validation across fields.
- Pick one save model per surface and make it obvious. **Autosave**: show "Saving…" then "Saved", and never also show a Save button. **Explicit save**: a Save button, a visible unsaved-changes indicator, and a warning before leaving with unsaved changes.

### Dashboards

- Start from the decisions users make ("Which accounts need attention today?"), then show the data that answers each one. Don't start from a row of KPI cards.
- A single number needs context to mean anything: comparison to a previous period or a target, and the time range.
- Choose the chart by the question:

| Question | Chart |
|---|---|
| Compare categories | Bar, sorted by value, horizontal if labels are long |
| Trend over time | Line; bars for few discrete periods |
| Part of a whole | Stacked bar or a single 100% bar; pie only for 2–4 slices |
| Distribution | Histogram, box plot, dot/strip plot |
| Relationship | Scatter |

- Label lines and bars directly at their ends instead of a distant legend when there are few series. Start bar axes at zero. Show units and time range.
- Color: categorical palettes for unordered categories (keep to a handful you can tell apart), sequential (one hue, light to dark) for ordered magnitude, diverging (two hues around a meaningful midpoint) for above/below a reference.
- NEVER rely on color alone to separate series or states: add labels, patterns, markers or position. Distinguish series by lightness as well as hue, so they survive color-vision deficiency and grayscale.
- Every chart has a text alternative: a summary sentence or an accessible data table.

### Settings

- Group by what users are trying to change, with a clear heading per group. Long settings use a section nav.
- Each setting: label, one line on what it affects, current value visible. Toggles apply immediately; grouped fields share one save.

### Destructive actions

- Prefer undo over confirmation for reversible actions ("Archived. Undo").
- Confirm only what can't be undone. The dialog names the object and the consequence ("Delete project 'Atlas'? 214 files will be removed permanently."), and the confirm button repeats the verb ("Delete project"). For high-stakes deletes, ask the user to type the name.
- Destructive buttons use the danger color plus a clear label; never the default focus in the dialog.

### Keyboard, command palette, notifications

- Offer shortcuts for frequent actions and show them in menus and tooltips. Don't override browser or assistive-technology shortcuts. Single-key shortcuts MUST be possible to turn off or remap, or work only when the relevant element has focus (WCAG 2.1.4).
- A command palette suits apps with many actions or objects; it searches both, shows shortcuts beside results, and opens with no animation, because keyboard-triggered UI should appear instantly (see `motion.md`).
- Notifications: confirm in place where the change is visible; use a toast only for background results or undo; reserve banners for persistent system state; never interrupt with a modal for information.

## Generic defaults to catch

- **A row of four gradient stat cards with icons and "+12%" badges** → the default dashboard opening, often with invented numbers → start from decisions; show context; NEVER invent figures.
- **Donut charts for everything** → hard to compare → pick the chart from the question table.
- **Centered numbers in tables, no tabular numerals** → digits don't line up → right-align with tabular numerals.
- **Every action as a primary button** → no hierarchy → one primary per page.
- **Rainbow chart palettes** → color without meaning → categorical, sequential or diverging on purpose.
- **Custom-styled dropdowns, toggles and date pickers** → novelty where people expect convention → native or established components.

## Check

- [ ] One primary action per page, in the header row.
- [ ] Numbers right-aligned with tabular numerals; text left-aligned.
- [ ] Long tables have sticky headers; truncated cells reveal the full value on hover and focus.
- [ ] Active filters visible with counts and "Clear all"; state in the URL.
- [ ] Empty, loading and error states exist for every table and chart.
- [ ] Each dashboard element answers a written question; each number has context.
- [ ] No chart relies on color alone; few series are labelled directly.
- [ ] Irreversible actions confirm with the object named; reversible ones offer undo.
- [ ] One save model per surface, clearly signalled.

# Color

Color sets mood before anything is read, and it carries state, emphasis and meaning. Choose how much color the page uses first, then which colors, then build them as a system.

## Decide

1. **Inherit.** Existing brand colors and tokens win (`extend.md`). Extend their ramps; don't replace them.
2. **Strategy.** Pick one of the four below for this surface's mode.
3. **Source.** List the colors of the subject's world: its objects, places, materials, the light it is used in, and for software its interface, states, signals and output. Pick from that list, not from what websites usually look like.
4. **Light or dark.** Decide from where and when the product is used (rules below), not from taste. Light grounds, warm off-whites included, are fine when the scene suits them; dark is never a way to look different.
5. **Build.** Ramps in OKLCH, tinted neutrals, semantic colors, tokens.
6. **Look.** Render the first screen and check it as a visitor would: a calm ground, text that reads easily, and one accent the eye goes to first. If the colors fight or shout, quiet them before adding anything.

## Strategy

| Strategy | What it is | Fits |
|---|---|---|
| **Restrained** | Tinted neutrals carry the page; one accent marks actions and state, under roughly 10% of the area | Operate by default; Read; Persuade when the content (photos, product) brings the color |
| **Committed** | One brand hue owns large surfaces (a header field, a section, the primary surfaces) plus neutrals | Persuade; Read for a brand with a strong owned color; Operate only in chrome (sidebar, header), never behind data |
| **Full palette** | Several hues, each with a fixed role (categories, products, characters, chart series) | When the subject has real categories, or the genre is plural (children's, food, events, editorial). Every hue needs a job |
| **Drenched** | One hue floods the whole view; text and surfaces are tones of that hue | Persuade only. Not for Operate or long Read |

AVOID mixing strategies within one surface. If you can't name the strategy, the page has none.

## Rules

- **SHOULD build ramps in OKLCH.** Its lightness channel is perceptually even, so equal L steps look like equal steps across hues, and changing L keeps the hue stable, which HSL does not (HSL yellow and blue at the same "lightness" look nothing alike).
- **SHOULD step lightness, not chroma, to make a ramp**, with 9–12 steps from near-white to near-black. Reduce chroma toward both ends: very light and very dark colors can't hold high chroma inside sRGB, and out-of-gamut values get clipped or mapped by the browser, often shifting hue. Check each step is in sRGB gamut; offer wider-gamut values only inside `@media (color-gamut: p3)`.
- **SHOULD tint neutrals toward the brand hue** with very low chroma (about 0.005–0.02). Grays, borders and dark surfaces then belong to the palette. Keep the tint consistent across the whole neutral ramp.
- **SHOULD ration the accent.** It marks the primary action, current selection, focus and key data, nothing decorative. One primary action per view. If everything is accented, nothing is.
- **SHOULD derive semantic colors in the same system.** Success, warning, danger and info get their own ramps at similar lightness and chroma to the brand ramp, so they sit in the palette rather than looking pasted in. If the brand hue is close to a semantic hue (a red brand, a green brand), separate them by hue shift, lightness and an icon or label, and never use the brand color for a destructive action.
- **NEVER carry meaning by color alone.** Pair status colors with text, icons or patterns; charts get labels or markers.
- **SHOULD choose light or dark from physical context.** Dim environments, long sessions at night, media and imaging, control rooms and terminals favour dark. Bright offices, outdoors, print-adjacent and long-form reading favour light. When both are supported, follow `prefers-color-scheme` and offer a manual switch.
- **Dark mode is a second design, not an inversion:**
  - SHOULD use a tinted, near-black base, not `#000`; pure black with white text smears on many displays.
  - SHOULD show elevation by lightness: raised surfaces are lighter. Shadows barely read on dark.
  - SHOULD lower chroma of large colored areas and accents compared to light mode; saturated color on dark vibrates.
  - SHOULD keep body text slightly below full white.
  - MUST re-check every contrast pair; ratios don't survive inversion.
  - SHOULD set `color-scheme` so form controls and scrollbars match.
- **MUST meet contrast** (table below) for text in every state, including placeholders, muted text, text on images and text on every point of a gradient. Disabled controls are exempt, but must still look disabled, not invisible.
- **Gradients need a purpose:** a light source, depth, a material, a transition between two real states. When used:
  - SHOULD stay same-hue or analogous (neighbouring hues). Distant hues need an intermediate stop.
  - SHOULD interpolate in a perceptual space: `linear-gradient(in oklch, …)` keeps chroma but can swing through unexpected hues between distant colors; `in oklab` takes the straight path with no hue swing, but can dip toward gray between near-complements. The default sRGB interpolation often produces a muddy middle.
  - SHOULD check banding on large, low-contrast gradients; a subtle noise layer or more stops fixes it.
- **MUST use tokens.** Two layers: primitive ramps (`--blue-600`) and semantic roles (`--color-surface`, `--color-text-muted`, `--color-accent`, `--color-danger`, `--color-border`). Components reference roles only; themes remap roles to different primitives.

## Values

| Pair | Minimum (WCAG 2.x AA) |
|---|---|
| Body and small text | 4.5:1 |
| Large text (24px+, or 19px+ bold) | 3:1 |
| UI component boundaries, focus indicators, icons that carry meaning, chart marks | 3:1 against adjacent colors |
| Enhanced (AAA) body text | 7:1 |

| OKLCH | Range |
|---|---|
| L | 0 to 1 (0% to 100%) |
| C | 0 up to about 0.37; most sRGB colors sit under 0.25 |
| H | 0–360 degrees |
| Neutral tint chroma | about 0.005–0.02 |

Contrast ratios are computed from relative luminance, not from OKLCH L; always measure the final pair.

## Generic defaults to catch

Palette tells live in `tells.md` (purple-blue gradients, glows, untinted neutrals, the safe "tasteful" palette, glass). Also catch:

- **The framework's default palette used as the brand** → recognisable instantly → build ramps from your source colors.
- **Accent on headings, icons, links, borders and buttons at once** → no hierarchy → ration it.
- **Semantic colors at full saturation next to a muted brand** → they shout → match lightness and chroma to the system.
- **Dark mode made by inverting light mode** → wrong elevation, harsh contrast → design it per the dark-mode rules.
- **Muted gray text that fails 4.5:1** → the most common contrast failure → darken until it passes.
- **Colored shadows and glows to add "depth"** → decoration → depth from lightness and layering; glow only where light has a source in the product.

## Check

- You can name the strategy and the subject source of each hue.
- Every color in the code is a token; components use role tokens only.
- One primary accent per view; it marks action or state, not decoration.
- All text pairs meet 4.5:1 (3:1 large); UI boundaries and focus meet 3:1, in light and dark.
- Status is readable in grayscale (icon or label present).
- Neutrals carry a consistent tint; no stray pure grays.
- Dark mode: no `#000` base, raised surfaces lighter, accents less saturated, form controls themed.
- Gradients have a stated purpose, a declared interpolation space, and no muddy or banded middle.

# Composition

How a page is put together: what the first screen does, what order the sections come in, and which skeleton carries them. Structure is the part of a design that two products most often share by accident; decide it, don't inherit it from habit.

## Decide

1. **What is the visitor's first question?** Usually one of: "what is this?", "does it work?", "is it for me?", "what does it cost?". The first viewport answers that one, and nothing else needs to.
2. **What must the first viewport do for this product?**
   - **Show** when the product is visual or easy to grasp on sight (tools, apps, physical goods, portfolios). The real thing, large, early.
   - **Claim** when the value is an idea the visitor must accept first (new category, service, policy). One concrete sentence, set with conviction.
   - **Set a mood** when the product is felt before it's understood (venues, fashion, music, hospitality). One real image or atmosphere, minimal text.
   - **Get to work** when the visitor already knows why they're here (docs, dashboards, search). The content or control itself, no preamble.
3. **What is the argument?** Write the sections as a list of questions the visitor asks in order, each answered by one section. If two sections answer the same question, merge them. If a question has no section, the page has a gap.
4. **Which skeleton fits that argument?** Pick from the vocabulary below, or combine two deliberately.
5. **How does it differ from the last build?** Check the variation axes.

## Page skeletons

| Skeleton | Shape | Fits when |
|---|---|---|
| **Demo-first** | Product UI or live example fills the first screen; text is a caption; sections walk through real use | The product sells itself on sight |
| **Long argument** | A single readable column of claim, evidence, objection, answer; few images | Complex or skeptical buyers; services, policy, technical depth |
| **Index** | A dense, scannable list or grid of items with filters; little intro | Catalogues, directories, templates, collections, changelogs |
| **Single statement** | One screen, one sentence, one action; maybe a short second screen | Waitlists, launches, events, personal sites |
| **Editorial** | Magazine rhythm: varied column widths, pull quotes, large images, chapters | Brands with a story and real material to show |
| **Comparison-led** | Opens with the choice the visitor is making (plans, before/after, us vs the old way) | Pricing pages, migrations, alternatives to an incumbent |
| **Timeline** | Sections ordered by time or process step, visibly sequenced | Processes, histories, onboarding, how something is made |
| **Document** | Looks like a well-set document: headings, numbered sections, footnotes, a contents list | Technical, legal, research or manifesto-like products |
| **Gallery-led** | Images carry the page; text is labels and captions | Photography, architecture, products bought on looks |
| **Tool-as-page** | The page is a working calculator, converter or demo; explanation sits below | Utilities, APIs, anything that can be tried without signing up |

## Variation axes

In New world work, consecutive builds SHOULD differ on at least two of these (the last build is whatever you can see: earlier in the conversation or `.gradientdeck/decisions.md`). Name the two in your design note. In Extend and New surface, inherit instead.

- **First viewport:** show, claim, mood, get to work; full-height vs partial; centered vs asymmetric.
- **Navigation:** top bar, side rail, inline contents list, minimal (logo + one action), none.
- **Section rhythm:** uniform blocks, alternating dense/sparse, one long flow, chapters with breaks.
- **Grid:** single column, two unequal columns, multi-column editorial, full-bleed with insets.
- **Image role:** evidence, atmosphere, explanation, none (see `imagery.md`).
- **Footer:** minimal line, sitemap, closing statement, contact block, none.

## Rules

- SHOULD let every section answer one question, and do one of four jobs: **explain** (what it is, how it works), **prove** (evidence for a claim), **deepen** (detail for people already convinced) or **convert** (the next step). A section that does none of these is cut, however good it looks.
- SHOULD vary section weight to match importance. The most persuasive section gets the most space; supporting detail gets less.
- SHOULD pass the **brand test** in Persuade mode: hide the logo and nav, then look at the first viewport. If it could belong to another company in the same category, the product's identity isn't in it yet; change the content or structure, not the decoration.
- AVOID filling the first viewport to exactly 100vh by default. Let the next section peek in when the page continues, so scrolling feels invited.
- SHOULD place proof next to the claim it supports, not in a separate "testimonials" band. NEVER invent it (see `SKILL.md`).
- SHOULD keep the page as short as the argument. Stop when the questions run out.

### Navigation

- SHOULD size the nav to the site: a five-page site needs no mega-menu; a single page may need only a logo and one action.
- MUST keep navigation reachable by keyboard, with the current page marked by more than color (see `accessibility.md`).
- SHOULD make sticky headers short and only sticky when the page is long enough to need them.
- On mobile, SHOULD keep the primary action visible outside the menu (see `responsive.md`).

### Calls to action

- SHOULD have one primary action per page, repeated where the argument resolves (after the key evidence and at the end), not after every section.
- SHOULD name the actual action (see `copy.md`). One secondary action at most beside it, visibly lower in weight.
- AVOID a closing full-width "Ready to get started?" band by default. End on the strongest evidence or a direct next step.

### Footers

- SHOULD match the footer to what visitors look for at the end: legal and contact for most sites, a sitemap only when there are enough pages to need one.
- AVOID four equal link columns, a newsletter box and social icons as the reflex footer.

## By mode

- **Persuade:** everything above applies. Structure is a primary place to be specific.
- **Operate:** follow app-shell conventions. Navigation in a side rail or top bar, consistent across screens; page title and primary action top of content; content fills the remaining space. Don't invent layouts per screen. See `apps-and-data.md`.
- **Read:** a reading column of 45–75 characters, generous margins, a contents list for long pages (sticky in the margin on wide screens), headings that work as an outline. Character goes in the margins, header and type, not in the column. See `typography.md`.
- **Extend / New surface:** inherit the existing nav, footer and section patterns. Decide only the order and skeleton of the new page (see `extend.md`).

## Generic defaults to catch

- **The default skeleton** (hero, three cards, testimonial, CTA band, footer) → no decision behind the order → write the visitor's questions, then choose a skeleton from the table.
- **Centered full-height hero with headline, subline, two buttons** → see `tells.md` → decide show / claim / mood / get to work first.
- **Every section the same height, padding and layout** → no hierarchy across the page → vary weight by importance.
- **Alternating image-left / image-right rows for every feature** → zig-zag filler → group features by the question they answer; show the few that matter.
- **Same nav and footer on every build** → the frame becomes a signature → choose them along with the skeleton.

## Check

- The first viewport answers one named visitor question, and you can say which.
- Each section maps to one question and one job (explain, prove, deepen, convert); no two answer the same one.
- Persuade: with logo and nav hidden, the first viewport still couldn't belong to a competitor.
- The skeleton is named in the design note, with the two variation axes that differ from the last build.
- One primary action, with a specific label, placed where the argument resolves.
- Nav and footer are sized to the site, keyboard-reachable, with current page marked.
- Operate screens share one shell; Read pages keep the column at 45–75 characters.

# Copy
